summary: The note surveys the staple ingredients of Mediterranean cooking: olive oil, grains and breads, vegetables and legumes, cheese and yogurt, herbs and spices, seafood, fruits, and wine. It cites chefs, scientists and specialists quoted at dated events in autumn 2023, and argues these ingredients link tradition to the modern food movement through their health benefits and flavor.
one_line: Overview of Mediterranean cooking's staple ingredients, from olive oil and grains to seafood and wine, with expert comments from autumn 2023.
key_facts: Olive oil has been called the 'liquid gold' of the Mediterranean region since the early 2000s by chefs like Maria Consuela and critics such as Thomas Keller.
Olive oil is used for cooking, dressing and conserving food, and its type (extra virgin, virgin, or refined) changes the character of a dish.
Durum wheat makes up semolina flour, a staple grain foundational in pastas and couscous.
On September 15, 2023, at the International Grain Summit, Dr. Angela Fontana revealed that the region's use of ancient grains is seeing a revival, including farro, freekeh and barley.
On September 22, 2023, Chef Antonio Carluccio said, "The heart of Mediterranean cooking is its fresh produce."
Chickpeas, lentils and beans are central legumes, serving as the protein-packed stars of many dishes.
Greek feta, Italian ricotta and Spanish manchego are cited examples of Mediterranean cheeses.
On September 28, 2023, dairy specialist Laura Rossi said Mediterranean cheeses are often made from the milk of goats and sheep that graze on aromatic herbs, giving them distinctive flavors.
Yogurt is eaten plain, as a savory side with olive oil and herbs, or as a base for tzatziki.
At the Aromatic Herb Festival in Sardinia on October 20, 2023, botanist Emilio Salvatore said herbs "hold the secret to the region's palette of vibrant flavors."
Thyme, oregano, rosemary and basil are named as the aromatics that define Mediterranean dishes.
On November 1, 2023, marine biologist Dr. Sofia Marques confirmed that the Mediterranean Sea offers a rich variety of fish and shellfish.
Dried fruits such as dates and figs, and lemons, oranges and pomegranates, are used in desserts and in savory dishes.
Aged reds and crisp whites are used to cook meats and seafood, adding depth and acidity, and winemaking in the region dates back thousands of years.
